explanations.explanation: That's the one, baker. The speaker says his commandments "…will add length to your days, years and peace to your life." Days AND peace in the same deal. That's a better package than anything I ever found in a junk drawer.

Fame sounds fun, friend, but the verse never mentions it. The speaker says the commandments "…will add length to your days, years and peace to your life." Nobody has to know your name in every land to have that.
Strong thought, but no battles show up in this verse. What the speaker promises is "…length to your days, years and peace to your life." So the answer is long days and peace, no armor needed.

explanations.answer: On the tablet of his heart
explanations.explanation: Right on, baker. The speaker says to "…write them on the tablet of your heart." So this isn't something you stick on the fridge. It goes deep, like a stamp pressed all the way into the dough.

explanations.answer: On the doorposts of his house
explanations.explanation: Doorposts do show up elsewhere in the Bible, in Deuteronomy 6:9, but not here. In this verse the speaker says to write them "…on the tablet of your heart." The writing goes inside the person, friend, not on the house.

explanations.answer: On a scroll in the temple
explanations.explanation: A scroll in the temple sounds official, friend, but that's not what this verse says. The speaker says to "…write them on the tablet of your heart." This one stays with you wherever you go, no trip to the temple needed.
Careful, baker, this one has a catch. The speaker says that holding on to these things brings "…favor and high regard in the sight of God and man." That's God AND people, so the answer is False.
Exactly. The speaker says you will find "…favor and high regard in the sight of God and man." Both are in there. He doesn't leave people out of the deal.
Yes, baker. The verse says, "…in all your ways acknowledge Him…" All your ways, not just the Sunday ones. I'd say that covers the Monday morning ones too, and I'm looking at myself with that one.
Questions are fine to bring, friend, but that's not the word here. The verse says, "…in all your ways acknowledge Him…" It's about owning that He's there, not putting Him on the witness stand.

Testing sounds like poking a cookie to see if it's done, friend, and that's not what this verse asks. It says, "…in all your ways acknowledge Him…" Acknowledging means recognizing Him, not checking whether He passes.

Close, but it's flipped, baker. The verse says, "…in all your ways acknowledge Him, and He will make your paths straight." The One doing the straightening is the LORD, so the answer is False. The son doesn't have to do it by himself.
That's it. The verse says, "…in all your ways acknowledge Him, and He will make your paths straight." He's the one who makes the paths straight. That's a lot less work for the son.

explanations.answer: Fear the LORD and turn from evil
explanations.explanation: Yes, baker. Instead of being wise in his own eyes, the son is told to "fear the LORD and turn away from evil." That's the swap: quit acting like you've got it all figured out and look up instead. I've read my own recipe, said "I know better," and had the dough set me straight.

explanations.answer: Praise the LORD and sing His name
explanations.explanation: Praising and singing are good things, friend, but they aren't what this verse says. The speaker says, "fear the LORD and turn away from evil." Those are the two.

explanations.answer: Serve the LORD and keep the Sabbath
explanations.explanation: Good things, baker, but not in this verse. Right after "Be not wise in your own eyes…" the speaker says, "fear the LORD and turn away from evil." There's no Sabbath in this line.

True, baker. Verse 7 says to "fear the LORD and turn away from evil." and verse 8 follows with, "This will bring healing to your body and refreshment to your bones." Healing and refreshment come right after. My old bones are listening.

It's actually True, friend. The speaker says to "fear the LORD and turn away from evil." and the very next verse says, "This will bring healing to your body and refreshment to your bones." It comes right after, no gap.

explanations.answer: They will be filled with plenty
explanations.explanation: Yes, baker. The speaker says, "…then your barns will be filled with plenty, and your vats will overflow with new wine." Full barns, overflowing vats. I'd call that a very full pantry.
Sturdy barns sound nice, friend, but the verse says nothing about how long they stand. It says, "…then your barns will be filled with plenty…" The barns are full, which beats a barn that's just old.

explanations.answer: They will be guarded from thieves
explanations.explanation: Nice thought, baker, but no thieves show up in this verse. The speaker says, "…then your barns will be filled with plenty…" The promise is about the barns being full, nothing about the lock on the door.

explanations.answer: The LORD disciplines the one He loves
explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. The speaker says, "…for the LORD disciplines the one He loves…" That's the reason he gives. The discipline comes with love, and that's worth remembering when it stings.

explanations.answer: The LORD rewards those who suffer quietly
explanations.explanation: The verse doesn't say that, friend. The reason given is, "…for the LORD disciplines the one He loves…" Nothing about suffering quietly. Honestly, I'm not a quiet sufferer, so I'm glad.

explanations.answer: The LORD's patience will soon run out
explanations.explanation: That's not in this verse, baker. The speaker's reason is, "…for the LORD disciplines the one He loves…" It's about love, and he doesn't say a word about patience running out.

True, baker. The verse says the LORD disciplines the one He loves, "…as does a father the son in whom he delights." A father who delights in his son and still disciplines him. I know a thing or two about that picture.
It's True, friend. The speaker says the LORD disciplines the one He loves, "…as does a father the son in whom he delights." That's the comparison, plain as flour on the counter.

Yes, baker. The speaker says wisdom "…is more profitable than silver, and her gain is better than fine gold." Then he says she's "…more precious than rubies…" Silver, gold and rubies all come in second.
Shiny, but not the word, friend. The speaker says her gain is "…better than fine gold." and that she's "…more profitable than silver…" It's about what wisdom is worth, not how much she sparkles.
Not quite, baker. The verse says wisdom's "…gain is better than fine gold." The comparison is about value, not strength. Gold never won an arm wrestle with anyone anyway.
That's right, baker. The verse says, "Long life is in her right hand; in her left hand are riches and honor." Wisdom shows up with both hands full.
Friends are a gift, but they aren't in this verse. It says, "Long life is in her right hand; in her left hand are riches and honor." Her right hand holds long life, friend.

Not in her hands, baker. The verse says, "Long life is in her right hand; in her left hand are riches and honor." Both hands are already full, and strength isn't in either one. I'd look for a third hand, but the verse only gives her two.
True, baker. The verse says, "All her ways are pleasant, and all her paths are peaceful." Pleasant AND peaceful, and the word is ALL both times. That's a good road.

It's True, friend, and I get why you hesitated. The question put peaceful up front, so pleasant can sneak right past you. But the verse says, "All her ways are pleasant, and all her paths are peaceful." (Proverbs 3:17) Both are in there, and ALL shows up twice, like a batch where every single cookie comes out right. Even I can't promise that one.

Yes, baker. The verse says, "The LORD founded the earth by wisdom…" The speaker has just been praising wisdom, and here the LORD founded the earth by it. The same verse says He "…established the heavens by understanding."

Strength is a fair guess, friend, but the verse says, "The LORD founded the earth by wisdom…" The word is wisdom, the very thing the speaker has been praising since verse 13. Strength isn't the word in this verse.
Fire makes for a dramatic guess, baker, but that's not the word. The verse says, "The LORD founded the earth by wisdom…" It's the same wisdom the speaker has been praising since verse 13.
Close, friend, but the word is different. The verse says, "By His knowledge the watery depths were broken open…" Broken open, not sealed shut, so the answer is False.
That's it, baker. The verse says, "By His knowledge the watery depths were broken open…" Not sealed shut. Then the clouds dripped with dew.
